raw_text:
Independent review of r-20261005T175306814457-ped-worker-threads at head 4302ec51 against base 23ee56ab (plan imas-ambix:project-environment-declared §5). §5 routes the 300 s-bound oversubscription to tests/conftest.py: each xdist worker caps its torch/OpenMP/MKL/OpenBLAS pools at its share of the CPUs available to the process, and a test checks the cap is set under xdist and absent without it. The node's two commits are c673667a (the cap, the shared stdlib module imas_ambix/_thread_pools.py, the oracle_probe refactor, the test file, the fragment) and 4302ec51 (reorders the cap to pin the environment before resolving torch, adds the ordering test, updates the fragment). The reviewed worktree is clean at 4302ec51; this review changed nothing in it.

Read the reviewed worktree at 4302ec51, its manifest, its r2 gate logs and its negative-control log, and the fragment, and reproduced the change in a scratch tree exported from the head (importing imas_ambix from the reviewed worktree via PYTHONPATH; module under test resolved to the reviewed tree's imas_ambix/_thread_pools.py). Reproduced: serial `pytest -p no:cacheprovider tests/test_worker_threads.py` -> 9 passed, 1 skipped, EXIT=0; `-n 4` -> 10 passed, EXIT=0; `-n 8` -> 10 passed, EXIT=0; `ruff check --no-cache imas_ambix tests` -> All checks passed!, EXIT=0. The declared negative control reproduces independently: moving _resolve_torch() ahead of pin_thread_pools() gives 1 failed, 9 passed under -n 4, the red test being test_environment_is_pinned_before_torch_is_resolved. Verified the ordering rationale: importing imas_ambix loads no numpy, torch or sklearn, so the pin lands before torch's runtimes load.

Gaps, all low severity, none blocking. (1) The cap's torch.set_num_threads branch is masked and untested: with the environment pinned before torch is imported, torch sizes its pool from the pin, so deleting the explicit call leaves the suite green -- measured here, the mutation `torch = _resolve_torch(); del torch` gives 10 passed, EXIT=0 under -n 4. The call is load-bearing only when torch was imported before conftest ran, and no test fires that path (the ordering test patches _resolve_torch to return None, the torch test runs after the pin). The node discloses this masking. (2) The session pool limiter global, entered once and never exited, would be rebound by a second real call and its __exit__ would restore the original pool sizes under GC; no current test reaches it. (3) The fragment ends without a trailing newline.

No added test failures: the reviewed manifest declares no baseline_suite/after_suite arms (both null) and its own head gate reports zero failures; the head tree re-run here reports 10 passed at -n 4 and -n 8 and 9 passed/1 skipped serial, so no failing id was added.
